body:
read the docs first so it can understand the abstraction

This is a pure research issue

agents.md will probably need to be changed

claimed: M5 session (Claude) · 2026-11-10T03:34Z · plan: research first, no branch yet. Answer the issue's open questions (whether to pin `solidcraft-ui-kit` or re-implement it, egui/wgpu version fit, layering and the command law, the component mapping, icons, snapshots) in comments. Then file the sub-issues. Questions for SolidCraft's side go to nateuax or jyviko on Discord.

## Research (agent, M5): answering #655's open questions

1. **Pin or re-implement? Pin, in stages.** SolidCraft's UI crates are built to be pinned by another app; that's solidcraft#14251's goal.
   - **Pinnable today:** the token crates `solidcraft-theme` and `solidcraft-color` (plus `ui-text`, `ui-registry` and the viewport crates).
   - **Not yet pinnable:** the components (`app_bar`, `ribbon`, `prefs_window`, `navigation_bar`, `history_bar`, `window_chrome`, `start_page`, `view_compass`). They still live in `solidcraft-ui-egui`. #14319 is merged, #14399 is open, and step 3 (extracting `crates/ui-kit`) is next.
   - **Not on crates.io** (`solidcraft-theme` "does not exist" there). So the pin is a git dependency at a rev or tag. Re-implementing would drift and double the work.
2. **egui / wgpu fit: a blocker today.** SolidCraft is on egui, eframe and egui-wgpu **0.37**, plus wgpu 30; CamCraft pins **=0.36.2**. One binary can't mix the two, so CamCraft bumps first: **#658**.
3. **Layering and the command law hold.** Per #14399 the kit components "take plain data and return what the user chose". CamCraft keeps the ui → app → flecs rule by turning each returned choice into a command, as today's panels do. No kit component writes app state.
4. **Mapping, as a first cut:**
   - workspace tabs (`TabTable`) ↔ CamCraft's Setup / 2D / 3D / Drill / Turn / Multi-axis / Sim / Post groups;
   - `history_bar` ↔ the operation list and undo history;
   - the browser tree ↔ the setup and operation tree;
   - `prefs_window` ↔ CamCraft's settings;
   - `app_bar` / `ribbon` / `window_chrome` ↔ the main toolbar and window.
5. **Icons:** the kit draws through a host-installed icon set (#14399), so CamCraft can keep its Tabler set (MIT) or adopt the kit's. That's a later sub-issue, decided with the components.
6. **Snapshots:** every pixel golden changes. They're regenerated once at the cut that lands the theme (AGENTS.md), and the structural twins carry the asserts in the PRs.

**Filed now:**
- **#658:** egui 0.37 bump (prerequisite).
- **#659:** theme tokens and tab accents from `solidcraft-theme` (the first visible step, pinnable today).

**To file once solidcraft#14251 step 3 ships `solidcraft-ui-kit`:**
- app bar, ribbon and window chrome;
- the Preferences window;
- tree and history mapping;
- icons.

**Questions for SolidCraft (nateuax or jyviko, Discord):**
- (a) Which ref should an outside app pin: a tag per SolidCraft release, or a rev?
- (b) Is there a timeline for #14251 step 3 (`crates/ui-kit`)?
- (c) Will the vendored `egui-wgpu` patch be needed by a pinning app too?

This umbrella stays open until the post-#14251 sub-issues are filed.

Filed **#661**: the icon set for the SolidCraft look, an enumerated checklist of about 60 new icons and about 20 conversions to SVG.
- **New:** operations, tool types, workspace tabs, tree rows, status badges and CamCraft actions.
- **Converted:** the existing original icons.

Generic chrome icons come from SolidCraft's own kit.

**On hold (contributor, 2026-11-09):** no agent works the SolidCraft UI changes (#655 and its sub-issues #658, #659, #661) until the maintainer has reviewed and signed off on the direction. Please don't pick or claim this until then. The maintainer may mark it `P?` (paused).

Maintainer answers:
Open question 1) We should  aim at pinning the Solidcraft UI bundle and retire our own completely. Early adoption is preferred and follow along with changes continuously.
Open question 2) We should layer Agents.md and refer to its UI agent from the main one. The sub agents.md should live with the UI crates as a steering document that gets ingested by the coding agent as a addendum to its agents file.

Question 3, 4, 5, 6 - use recommendation rule from Agents.md - we use recommendation, document it and move with its changes.

## Estimate and proposed breakdown (agent, for the maintainer, 2026-11-12)

**Verdict:** as an umbrella this is `effort:max` (open design; about 20-25 PRs beyond #658, #659 and #661). It should be worked as research plus sub-issues, never as one issue. **One finding comes before any estimate: the crates this issue wants to pin are no longer MIT OR Apache-2.0.** This is a read-only estimate: nothing was built, filed, labelled or claimed.

### 1. Licence: changed two days ago, and it blocks the pin
- **What changed.** SolidCraft commit `312454f899` (2026-11-10 14:06 UTC, their pull request 14578) added `LICENSE-BRAND`, the "SolidCraft Brand and Interface Licence". It covers `crates/ui-kit`, `crates/look` (the interface icon masters, glyphs and built-in themes) and `crates/theme`. Their manifests now say `license-file = "LICENSE"`, and `NOTICE`, `README.md` and `ATTRIBUTION.md` (425 files under `crates/look`) say the same.
- **What it asks.** Clause 3a needs the maintainers' written permission for "Using any Brand Material in another program, product, service or library, including linking to the UI kit, the look or the theme from software that is not SolidCraft". The preamble says a program built from SolidCraft's open code "should not look like SolidCraft unless the maintainers have agreed". That is this issue's goal.
- **Still MIT OR Apache-2.0:** `solidcraft-color` (140 lines), `ui-text`, `ui-registry` and the viewport crates. None of them is the look.
- **Earlier versions.** Clause 5 leaves versions published before the licence under their old one. The last tree before the change is `a347568301` (2026-11-10 12:48 UTC), where `ui-kit` and `theme` carry the workspace licence. Staying on that tree is the opposite of "follow its changes continuously", and whether to lean on it at all is a legal call for the maintainer, not for an agent.
- **Others are asking.** Two permission requests are open upstream with no answer yet (their issues 14690, from a sibling app in the same organisation, and 14898).
- **Our side.** AGENTS.md "Assets" admits MIT, ISC, Apache-2.0 and BSL only, so a permission-based licence needs a rule change. The texts of #655, #659 and #661 that say "Apache-2.0, keep the NOTICE" are out of date. #661 is in work, and its plan to borrow about 30 SolidCraft SVGs meets the same licence (the masters moved into `crates/look`); the main session has been told.

**So the first step is the maintainer's:** ask SolidCraft for written permission to use `ui-kit`, `look` and `theme` in CamCraft (source, releases, web build, forks, and which revisions), and decide the AGENTS.md rule. Apart from the rows marked "today" below, nothing should start before that answer is in the repo.

### 2. Upstream facts (checked today; SolidCraft `main` = `9fd103a0f3`, v0.40.1)
- **The kit exists.** `solidcraft-ui-kit` landed on 2026-11-10, and their tracking issue 14251 is closed as completed. It is 102 Rust files, 2.4 MB (about 55-60k lines): ribbon, app bar, window chrome, Preferences window, panels, menus, tree rows, form rows, history bar, navigation bar, view compass, start page, toasts and theme files. `solidcraft-look` (icons, glyphs, IBM Plex under OFL 1.1, built-in themes) and `solidcraft-theme` (about 3k lines) sit beside it.
- **Stack.** egui, eframe and egui-wgpu 0.37.0; wgpu 30.0.1; winit 0.30.13; Rust 1.95. It has no `egui_dock` and no `egui_kittest`.
- **Not light to build.** `ui-kit` depends on `solidcraft-viewport-egui` and `solidcraft-viewport-gpu`, which pull `solidcore-record` and `solidcore-tess` (about 1 MB of Rust) from SolidCraft's vendored kernel. Our `crates/kernel` pins `solidcore = "=1.0.1"` from crates.io, so kernel code would be compiled twice, from two sources.
- **It needs SolidCraft's patched egui-wgpu.** The kit's `blur_native.rs` uses `egui_wgpu::DeviceLost`, `capture_errors` and `FrameCompositor`. They are in SolidCraft's `vendor/egui-wgpu` (205 KB) and not in egui-wgpu 0.37.0. A pinning app adds a `[patch.crates-io]` entry for it. That answers the earlier question (c): yes.
- **Pin form.** Nothing is on crates.io (`solidcraft-theme`, `-ui-kit`, `-look` and `-color` all answer 404). The pin is a git `rev` or tag of the whole repository, which GitHub reports at 521 MB. Cargo clones it once per machine and once per `release.yml` run.
- **Cadence.** At least 40 release tags in the last 29 days (v0.13.0 on 2026-10-15 to v0.40.1 today); more than 100 commits on `main` in the last 24 hours; 17 commits touched `crates/ui-kit` in its first three days. Following it needs a routine. I propose one pin bump a week, or one per non-rc tag, whichever comes later.

### 3. Our side (measured on `main`)
`crates/ui` is 62.3k lines in 246 files:

| Part | Lines | Files | Under the kit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chrome: shell, dock, ribbon, tree, window chrome, form helpers, view cube | 7.5k | 26 | replaced |
| Theme and colour | 2.1k | 8 | replaced (#659), except the verdict palette and its maths |
| CAM pages and dialogs | 11.7k | 54 | restyled |
| Viewport, wgpu, scene | 5.3k | 20 | kept; how it sits under the panels is the open design |
| State and interaction law | 12.0k | 40 | kept |
| Tests, in the crate and in `tests/` | 19.0k + 4.7k | 83 + 14 | 665 tests; each one that finds a widget by label or role is exposed |

- **The pages have a seam.** 245 `prop_row` and 39 `check_row` calls go through `layout/form.rs`, so they can move to kit rows in one place. About 290 raw widget calls and 315 labels do not go through it.
- **The shell differs in kind.** Ours is `egui_dock` tabs with the viewport as an offscreen texture in a tab (`register_native_texture`), our own winit loop and `egui_wgpu::Renderer` on native, and eframe on the web. SolidCraft has no dock library: its panels are cards over a full-window viewport drawn in paint callbacks, with a blur that wants an `egui_wgpu::RenderState`. Adopting the kit completely replaces `egui_dock` (`layout/mod.rs`, `shell.rs`, and as a type in `shell_window.rs`, `shell_web.rs`, `tests.rs`).
- **Tests.** Ours use egui_kittest and AccessKit: 185 `Harness` uses in 40 files, and `structural.rs` is 309 lines. The kit names its widgets through `solidcraft_ui_registry` and calls `widget_info` rarely (12 times in the 2,063 lines of its `fields.rs`). Whether our label and role asserts still find kit controls is unknown.
- **Pixel goldens.** There are only 3 PNGs. They are regenerated once at the cut, so that risk is small.
- **400-line law.** The kit's own files run to 2,000 lines, but they are a dependency. Our adapters stay under 400. `panes.rs` (1,516) and `shell.rs` (960) are over the limit today, and the swap is when they go.
- **Actions budget.** No trigger changes. The cost shows only in `release.yml` on a tag: a bigger clone and more crates to compile, with Windows billed double.

### 4. Size, and what is a guess
About 20-25 PRs after #658 and #659, touching 25-40% of `crates/ui` (15-25k changed lines, much of it deletion and test rework). **That range is a guess.** The spike in row 4 below would firm it up. It is a throwaway host window with the kit's app bar, ribbon and Preferences over our viewport, on native and wasm. It answers:
- whether the patched egui-wgpu and a `RenderState` are forced on our native shell;
- the build-time and binary cost of the second kernel copy;
- how kit controls show up in kittest.

### 5. Proposed sub-issues, in build order

| # | Title | Done means | Effort | Areas | Depends on | Start |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Maintainer: written permission from SolidCraft for `ui-kit`, `look`, `theme` | the grant (scope, revisions, conditions) is recorded in `docs/decisions/` and quoted in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` | maintainer's own | - | - | today, maintainer only |
| 2 | Process: UI steering document `crates/ui/AGENTS.md`, referenced from the root file | the UI laws (layering, command law, form seam, tests, snapshots) live there; the root links it; the path is in the fork sync list; `PROCESS_VERSION` bumped | `effort:low` | `documentation`, `area:ui` | - | today |
| 3 | Process: admit the SolidCraft UI bundle in "Assets" and "Dependencies" | the exception names the three crates and the permission record; `PROCESS_VERSION` bumped | `effort:low` | `documentation` | 1 | waits on 1 |
| 4 | Research: spike host window on the kit (throwaway) | a comment here with the patch answer, the `RenderState` answer, build time and binary size, kittest visibility, and the wasm result; nothing merges | `effort:high` | `area:ui`, `area:build` | 1, #658 | waits |
| 5 | Build: pin `ui-kit`, `look`, `ui-text`, `ui-registry` by rev; patch egui-wgpu; install the look | one egui in `cargo tree`; the app and the tests start with the look installed; notices (brand licence with the permission, OFL for Plex) in `LICENSES.md` | `effort:high` | `area:build`, `area:ui` | 4, #659 | waits; `needs-maintainer` |
| 6 | Tooling: pin-and-follow routine (`cargo xtask ui-pin` or a skill) | one command lists upstream commits to the pinned crates since our rev, bumps the rev, runs the ui gate and opens a draft PR; the steering document states the weekly rhythm | `effort:medium` | `area:build` | 5 | waits |
| 7 | Tests: harness on the kit | the test context installs the look; the structural helpers find kit controls; `structural.rs` green | `effort:high` | `area:ui` | 5 | waits |
| 8 | UI: window chrome and app bar from the kit | title row, menus and window controls are the kit's; every choice maps to an existing command; `window_chrome.rs` gone | `effort:high` | `area:ui` | 7 | waits |
| 9 | UI: ribbon from the kit | operation groups are ribbon data; icons come through the host icon set (#661); the painted ribbon in `panes.rs` and `painted.rs` gone | `effort:high` | `area:ui` | 7, #661 | waits |
| 10 | UI: panel layout replaces `egui_dock` | browser and properties are kit panels around the viewport; viewport input unchanged; `egui_dock` out of `Cargo.toml` and `LICENSES.md` | `effort:max` | `area:ui`, `area:build` | 8 | waits |
| 11 | UI: browser tree on kit tree rows | the setup and operation tree draws with the kit's rows; the radio still queues `ActivateSetup`; context menus kept | `effort:high` | `area:ui` | 10 | waits |
| 12 | UI: form seam on kit rows | `layout/form.rs` and `fields.rs` draw through kit rows; the 284 call sites follow without edits | `effort:medium` | `area:ui` | 7 | waits |
| 13 | UI: pages draw only through the form seam (7 PRs, one per page family) | no raw `ui.button`, `checkbox`, `label` or `add` left in that family's pages; a guard test counts them | `effort:medium` each | `area:ui` | - | today (ours either way) |
| 14 | UI: Preferences window from the kit | theme, colour vision, GPU and unit choices live in it; each is a command with its MCP tool | `effort:high` | `area:ui`, `area:mcp` | 8 | waits |
| 15 | UI: dialogs, prompts and toasts on kit containers (2 PRs) | the unsaved prompt, post refusal, fixture and machine dialogs and the G-code window use kit containers | `effort:medium` | `area:ui` | 12 | waits |
| 16 | UI: view compass and navigation bar replace `viewcube.rs` | same pick law and camera commands; `viewcube.rs` gone | `effort:high` | `area:ui` | 10 | waits |
| 17 | UI: history bar over the operation list and undo history | the bar shows the command history; a click undoes or redoes through the history, never around it | `effort:high` | `area:ui`, `area:mcp` | 10 | waits |
| 18 | Cleanup: retire the leftovers | `painted.rs`, the PNG icon loader, unused PNGs and their notices are gone; the snapshot refresh is listed for the cut | `effort:medium` | `area:ui` | 8-17 | waits |

The page families of row 13 are: 2D, 3D, holes, turning, multi-axis, setup and fixtures, tools and machine.

**Order across the three issues:** permission (row 1), then #658, then #659, then rows 4-18. Rows 2 and 13 and the "today" rows of #658 and #659 need nothing from upstream.

**Top risks:**
1. No permission, or one with conditions we cannot meet. Then this issue becomes "a look of our own", and rows 5-12 and 14-17 are redrawn as CamCraft-own work.
2. The shell change (row 10): the viewport, its input routing and the wasm shell all pass through it.

**Labels:** this issue carries both `P2` and `P?`. AGENTS.md says `P?` stands instead of a priority, so one of them is for the maintainer to remove. The same holds for #658 and #659.

**Maintainer decisions (question dialog, 2026-11-12)**
1. Direction: **ask SolidCraft's maintainers for written permission, and keep #655, #658 and #659 paused until they answer** (their `LICENSE-BRAND` of 2026-11-10 requires it for `ui-kit`, `look` and `theme`). Not chosen: building on the last MIT/Apache revision (it could never follow upstream), and dropping the adoption.
2. Breakdown: only the sub-issues that are useful whatever the answer is are filed, at `P2`: #1118 (trial bump to egui 0.37, part of #658), #1119 (accessible name on every input widget, part of #658), #1120 (no colour literals outside the token table, part of #659), #1121 (UI steering document `crates/ui/AGENTS.md`), #1122 (pages draw only through the form seam). The rest of the breakdown stays as the proposal in the estimate comments.
3. #661 (our own icon set) is open at `P1` and takes nothing from SolidCraft.

Permission request posted upstream on the maintainer's word (2026-11-12): tangency-labs/solidcraft issue 15340 (https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/issues/15340). It asks for written permission under LICENSE-BRAND section 3a to use `ui-kit`, `theme` with the colour crate, and `look` from CamCraft, pinned by revision, and whether the grant covers future revisions. #655, #658 and #659 stay paused until it is answered; the answer (scope, revisions, conditions) goes into `docs/decisions/` and `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`.

Checked before posting: SolidCraft's UI crates still live in its main repo (no separate UI repo in that organisation). A different, permissively licensed shared kit exists - `craft-ui` in storytold/craft-libs (MIT OR Apache-2.0, egui 0.37, controls and a docking surface, no icons or themes bundled; SolidCraft does not depend on it) - not evaluated yet.
